findings.quote: Marcos was silent, tapping his stick twice against the leg of his chair—not tapping it to say something, just tapping it the way he did when he was thinking.
findings.claim: Canon gives the two taps one trigger: about to tell the truth. The draft spends them on idle thinking and says so outright, which tells the reader the signal is not a signal.
findings.fix: Remove the tapping from this scene, or restructure it so Marcos taps in a context consistent with canon.
findings.reference: bible/characters.md, Marcos — 'taps his walking stick twice against the ground when about to tell the truth'

iterations.notes: One high-severity contradiction. Everything else canon-compliant: names, Day 5 afternoon/evening, Bruno's three circles and the foot of the bed, R5 supper, the notebook given Day 1 with its first entry a question never answered, the fossil and the stone.

The Marcos contradiction is resolved: 'Marcos was silent in his corner, one hand resting on his walking stick, his eyes on [NOMBRE_ANONIMIZADO]' keeps him present and watchful with the signal unspent. The two prose replacements introduce no canon conflict.

The restored beat-2 paragraph describes Bruno as tail straight, ears forward, body no longer coiled — consistent with characters.md. Bruno still circles three times and sleeps at the foot of the bed. No name drift, no timeline conflict, all four mysteries remain closed.
